title: What does XLS-64 specify for Pseudo-accounts?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-64 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-64 describes pseudo-accounts used by protocol-managed ledger features rather than ordinary user signers. [1]

A pseudo-account supports the state and balances of a feature such as a vault. It should not be treated as a conventional wallet whose operator can simply sign an arbitrary Payment. Applications must inspect the associated feature object and its permitted transactions. An account-shaped ledger entry does not imply the same control model as an externally managed key pair. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-64 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Draft. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-64 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
